issues.description: Default extraction points at data/stories, but the repository contains no story manifest or story files, so the documented demo fails.
Story loading hard-fails on missing corpus files with no built-in generator, fixture fallback, or actionable setup path.
The tiny end-to-end test is not self-contained and currently fails against a clean checkout.
The documented tiny CPU demo commands do not work because required input data is not included or generated.
The installed console script defaults to external config/data paths that are not packaged, making normal package usage fragile.
Config values are coerced but not validated, allowing empty emotion lists, zero topic counts, bad layer fractions, and negative token starts to fail later.
Extraction assumes every configured emotion has data and matching shapes, so partial or invalid inputs crash with low-context NumPy or KeyError failures.
Full-model extraction runs every story serially with no batching, truncation, checkpointing, or progress handling, making the configured scale brittle.
Validation loads vector artifacts but instantiates the backend from current CLI flags instead of enforcing the backend/model recorded in the manifest.
Preference steering can silently pair saved vectors with a different runtime backend/model because manifest compatibility is not checked.
Saved vector arrays are loaded without shape, dtype, finite-value, emotion-count, or layer-count validation.
Preference validation trusts artifact shape and can compute invalid correlations or crash late when vectors do not match the manifest/backend.
The HuggingFace preference score is based on a single good-minus-bad next-token logit after a numeric-score prompt, which is not a reliable preference measurement.
HuggingFace activation extraction has no max-length handling, so longer inputs can exceed context limits or cause avoidable memory failures.
Model loading uses default full-precision placement for dtype auto and no device_map or memory options, which is risky for the documented 2B model path.
pca_components_for_variance returns one component for threshold 0 instead of zero components.
Negative token_start values are accepted and interpreted as Python negative slicing rather than rejected.
Tiny backend emotion matching uses substring counts, which can create false-positive or overlapping lexical signals.
Dependencies are lower-bounded but unpinned, leaving the project vulnerable to future NumPy, Matplotlib, PyYAML, torch, or transformers breakage.
The demo writes into the repository outputs tree by default, which mutates checked-out sample artifacts and fails in read-only checkouts.
